content.summary: Reference list entries focusing on heart failure outcomes, ventricular arrhythmia risk, impact of renal dysfunction and diabetes on sudden cardiac death, clinical trial baseline characteristics (GALACTIC-HF), acid-base and electrolyte abnormalities in heart failure, management of hyperkalaemia with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) including RALES and EMPHASIS-HF trials, and long-term potassium monitoring.

references.citation: Goldenberg I, Younis A, Aktas MK, McNitt S, Zareba W, Kutyifa V. Competing risk analysis of ventricular arrhythmia events in heart failure patients with moderately compromised renal dysfunction. Europace 2020;22:1384-1390.
clinical_points: Examines competing risks for ventricular arrhythmia events in heart failure patients with moderate renal dysfunction.
Highlights interplay between renal function and arrhythmic risk in heart failure.

references.citation: Coiro S, Girerd N, Sharma A, Rossignol P, Trittto I, Pitt B, Pfeffer MA, McMurray JJV, Ambrosio G, Dickstein K, Moss AJ, Zannad F. Association of diabetes and kidney function according to age and systolic function with the incidence of sudden cardiac death and non-sudden cardiac death in myocardial infarction survivors with heart failure. Eur J Heart Fail 2019;21:1248-1258.
clinical_points: Analyzes how diabetes and kidney function, stratified by age and systolic function, relate to incidence of sudden and non-sudden cardiac death in MI survivors with heart failure.
Emphasizes diabetes and renal dysfunction as important risk modifiers for mortality modes in heart failure.

references.citation: Teerlink JR, Diaz R, Felker GM, McMurray JJV, Metra M, Solomon SD, Adams KF, Anand I, et al. Omecamtiv mecarbil in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: GALACTIC-HF baseline characteristics and comparison with contemporary clinical trials. Eur J Heart Fail 2020;22:2160-2171.
clinical_points: Presents baseline characteristics of GALACTIC-HF trial of omecamtiv mecarbil in HFrEF.
Provides comparisons with other contemporary heart failure clinical trials.

references.citation: Urso C, Brucculeri S, Caimi G. Acid-base and electrolyte abnormalities in heart failure: pathophysiology and implications. Heart Fail Rev 2015;20:493-503.
clinical_points: Reviews pathophysiology and clinical implications of acid-base and electrolyte disturbances in heart failure.
Relevant for managing metabolic and electrolyte derangements in HF patients.

references.citation: Butler J, Vijayakumar S, Pitt B. Need to revisit heart failure treatment guidelines for hyperkalaemia management during the use of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. Eur J Heart Fail 2018;20:1247-1251.
clinical_points: Argues for reassessment of HF guidelines concerning hyperkalemia management when using MRAs.
Highlights clinical dilemma of balancing MRA benefits with risk of hyperkalaemia.

references.citation: Vardeny O, Claggett B, Anand I, Rossignol P, Desai AS, Zannad F, Pitt B, Solomon SD, Randomized Aldactone Evaluation Study (RALES) Investigators. Incidence, predictors, and outcomes related to hypo- and hyperkalemia in patients with severe heart failure treated with a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist. Circ Heart Fail 2014;7:573-579.
clinical_points: Reports incidence, predictors, and outcomes of hypo- and hyperkalemia in severe HF patients treated with MRAs (RALES data).
Provides evidence on electrolyte disturbances associated with spironolactone therapy.

references.citation: Rossignol P, Dobre D, McMurray JJ, Swedberg K, Krum H, van Veldhuisen DJ, Shi H, Messig M, Vincent J, Girerd N, Bakris G, Pitt B, Zannad F. Incidence, determinants, and prognostic significance of hyperkalemia and worsening renal function in patients with heart failure receiving the mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist eplerenone or placebo in addition to optimal medical therapy: EMPHASIS-HF. Circ Heart Fail 2014;7:51-58.
clinical_points: Analyzes hyperkalemia and worsening renal function incidence and prognostic significance in HF patients on eplerenone (EMPHASIS-HF).
Addresses safety considerations of eplerenone in addition to standard therapy.

references.citation: Nunez J, Bayes-Genis A, Zannad F, Rossignol P, Nunez E, Bodi V, Minana G, Santas E, Chorro FJ, Mollar A, Carratala A, Navarro J, Gorriz JL, Lupon J, Husser O, Metra M, Sanchis J. Long-term potassium monitoring and dynamics in heart failure and risk of mortality. Circulation 2018;137:1320-1330.
clinical_points: Investigates long-term potassium monitoring, potassium dynamics, and association with mortality risk in heart failure.
Supports ongoing surveillance of potassium levels in HF management.

key_topics: Ventricular arrhythmia risk in heart failure with renal dysfunction
Interaction of diabetes and renal function with sudden cardiac death risk
GALACTIC-HF trial baseline characteristics for omecamtiv mecarbil
Electrolyte and acid-base disturbances in heart failure
Hyperkalaemia risks and management with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (spironolactone, eplerenone)
Incidence and prognostic impact of hypo- and hyperkalemia in RALES and EMPHASIS-HF
Importance of long-term potassium monitoring in heart failure
